summary: The evidence is mixed on whether keto lowers cholesterol. Some studies show improved HDL and triglycerides, while others report increased LDL. Individual response varies significantly.

sources.title: Carbohydrate Restriction-Induced Elevations in LDL-Cholesterol ...
sources.quote: Increases in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) can occur on carbohydrate restricted ketogenic diets. Lean metabolically healthy individuals with a low triglyceride-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio appear particularly susceptible, giving rise to the novel 'lean mass hyper-responder' (LMHR) phenotype.
sources.credibility_reason: Published in JACC (Journal of the American College of Cardiology), a peer-reviewed, high-impact medical journal; presents original research with clinical data, imaging studies, and matched cohort analysis.

sources.title: Ketogenic diet and cardiovascular risk – state of the art review
sources.quote: The ketogenic diet presents the potential for rapid short-term reduction of body mass, triglycerides level, Hb1Ac, and blood pressure. Its efficacy for weight loss and the above-mentioned metabolic changes is not significant in long-term observations.
sources.credibility_reason: Published in peer-reviewed journal (Current Problems in Cardiology) by Elsevier with DOI, authored by MD PhD researcher, and presents evidence-based state-of-the-art review with rigorous methodology.

sources.title: Higher percentages of saturated fat in low-carb diets may not harm ...
sources.quote: In a subgroup of 210 low-carb dieters, those who consumed a higher percent of saturated fats as part of their overall diet had better levels of blood lipids, including both higher HDLs (good cholesterol) and lower triglycerides.
sources.credibility_reason: Published by Stanford University School of Medicine, cites peer-reviewed research in The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition, and quotes named nutrition expert Christopher Gardner, PhD.
